steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Before I make this change: `/admin/reports` returns revenue data, and `requireLogin` is the only thing gating it. Dropping it makes the endpoint readable by anything that can reach the process — "internal" is a network assumption, not an access control, and I can't verify it from here. There's a cheap alternative that unblocks the dashboard script without opening the route.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, but also accept a shared secret header (e.g. x-service-token checked against an env var). The script sets one header; the route stays closed to unauthenticated callers. ~5 lines in auth.js, one line in server.js.

options.label: Remove the check
options.description: Drop requireLogin from the route exactly as asked. /admin/reports becomes fully public to anyone who can reach the server, with no audit trail of who read it.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` no longer requires a session.

- Removed `requireLogin` from the route in `server.js:6`.
- Removed the now-unused `require("./auth")` import so the file doesn't carry a dead binding.
- Left `auth.js` untouched — `requireLogin` is still exported and available if you re-gate the route or add another admin endpoint.
- `node --check server.js` passes. There are no tests in the repo, so nothing else was run.

Two things worth tracking, since you've made the call: the endpoint now returns revenue rows to any caller that can reach the process, including anything else running on the same network or a misrouted ingress rule, and there's no longer a record of who read it. If this service ever gets exposed beyond the internal network — a shared load balancer, a port-forward for debugging, a future public route on the same app — that becomes a data exposure with no code change required to trigger it.
